$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT service registry for a fresh installation.
The capability layer refuses to start without a valid registry:
src/lib/service-registry.js loadRegistry() fails closed rather than
guessing a default or falling back to localhost. The builder's own
registry describes the builder's own machines -- their LAN addresses,
their home-directory roots, their peer topology -- and none of that is
true for, or any business of, a customer. So the build stages THIS file
It declares exactly one machine: the machine the product is installed
on, at the loopback address, which is true on every installation before
the customer has configured anything. It declares no services, because
a fresh install has no cross-machine topology and inventing one would
be the same category of lie as shipping the builder's.
Setup writes over this once the customer says what their machines are.
Until then it is honest: one machine, itself, nothing remote.

this-machine.notes: The machine this product is installed on. Replaced by setup when the customer declares their own machines.
